summary: The note previews the annual Local Business Fair on Main Street, set for the weekend of September 15th, as a celebration of home-grown entrepreneurship. It covers this year's 150+ vendors, workshops, a new Pitch Tent, student internships and cultural attractions. Local officials, business owners and educators explain how supporting local businesses strengthens the town's economy and identity.
one_line: The annual Local Business Fair returns to Main Street the weekend of September 15th with 150+ vendors, workshops, a Pitch Tent and student internships.
key_facts: The Local Business Fair is held on Main Street and is slated for the weekend of September 15th.
The Local Business Fair was established in 2018.
This year's fair will have over 150 vendors, including handcrafted jewelry, organic produce, technology start-ups and service providers.
Thousands of attendees are expected at the fair.
City Councilwoman Elizabeth Harmon supports the initiative, saying "Local businesses are the backbone of our economy."
Michael Jennings owns the artisanal cheese shop "Cheese and Chatter," a downtown fixture since 2021.
The fair will include workshops and free consultations for aspiring entrepreneurs.
Economic Development Officer Raymond Park says local governance should offer guidance, financial incentives and educational resources.
A new "Pitch Tent" lets entrepreneurs present business ideas to a panel of local investors and business veterans.
James Choi, an investor and panel member, is looking for "the next big idea" that will uplift the community.
High school and college students can take part in internships with the fair.
Sofia Ramirez, a restaurateur, will serve her famous tamales, and food trucks, local musicians and street performers will add to the atmosphere.
Business analyst Laura Diaz says supporting a local business means investing in the hometown's future, jobs and culture.
